subject: Communication
title: The Caucus: Private Conversations in Mediation
description: A quick, practical guide to The Caucus: Private Conversations in Mediation.

hook.text: The mediator calls a break and speaks to each side privately. In ten minutes, a deadlock that lasted hours dissolves.

buildup.text: A caucus is a private, confidential session between the mediator and one party during a mediation process.

discovery.text: People say things in private they won't say in front of the other party — fears, real interests, flexibility.

twist.text: Caucuses are controversial. Some mediators avoid them because they can create suspicion about what was said privately.

climax.text: Used skillfully, caucuses unlock hidden flexibility. Used poorly, they breed distrust.

punchline.text: Sometimes resolution starts with a private conversation.

quiz.question: What is a caucus in mediation?
options: A private session between mediator and one party

details.summary: A caucus is a private session between the mediator and one party during a mediation. It allows each side to share sensitive information, vent emotions, and explore options without the pressure of the other party watching. Caucuses often unlock breakthroughs.
details.whyItMatters: Caucuses reveal information people will not share in joint sessions. Many mediations succeed because of what happens in these private conversations.
takeaways: A caucus is a private meeting with one party during mediation
It allows safe venting and exploration of hidden interests
Confidentiality in caucuses is essential for trust

faq.question: Does the mediator share caucus information with the other party?
faq.answer: Only with explicit permission. What is said in caucus is confidential by default. The mediator may ask, 'May I share this with the other side?' This confidentiality is what makes people willing to reveal their true concerns and flexibility in private.

faq.question: When should a mediator call a caucus during a session?
faq.answer: When emotions escalate beyond productive levels, when one party seems unable to speak freely, when a confidential exploration of options would help, or when the mediator senses hidden information. Experienced mediators develop intuition for the right moment.
